steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: HFD vs chow
steps.question: Which of the 12000 mouse liver genes are differentially expressed between high-fat diet (n=6) and chow (n=6) mice, using DESeq2 with chow as the reference level?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, minimal pre-filter, BH+independent filtering at alpha 0.05, explicit reference level (chow); low-depth sample_01 is retained and its contribution down-weighted through its size factor (R-0030) rather than removed by default.

steps.description: Pre-filter to genes with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (the smaller group size). Build DESeq2 design ~condition with condition releveled so chow is the reference. Run DESeq() (median-of-ratios size factors, Wald test). Extract results with alpha=0.05 and independent filtering on, apply apeglm shrinkage to log2FoldChange for the condition_HFD_vs_chow coefficient. Report both unshrunken and shrunken log2FC with lfcSE, BH-adjusted p-values, inspect and report the raw p-value histogram shape, and flag any gene with an NA p-value from Cook's-distance outlier detection separately from independent-filtering NAs. Produce MA plot and dispersion plot as fit diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Design formula ~condition with chow set as explicit reference level; contrast named condition_HFD_vs_chow
Results table has raw and apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue, padj for every tested gene
Number of genes tested after filtering and number significant at padj<0.05 reported
MA plot, dispersion plot, and p-value histogram produced
Genes with NA padj distinguished as Cook's-outlier-flagged vs independent-filtering-excluded

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on Hallmark gene sets (mouse)
steps.question: Which of the MSigDB mouse Hallmark pathways are enriched (up or down) between high-fat diet and chow liver, using the full ranked gene list from the DESeq2 contrast?

grounding.reason: Mouse dataset uses the mouse-specific MSigDB Hallmark collection (present in the reference store as mh.all.v2026.1.Mm.symbols.gmt), ranked preranked fgsea on the Wald statistic (chosen side of the disputed ranking-metric rule R-0108), full ranked list, 15-500 size window, redundant sets collapsed.

steps.description: Rank all genes tested in the DESeq2 HFD-vs-chow contrast by their Wald statistic (stat column, signed and SE-scaled) with no significance cutoff applied. Run fgsea against the MSigDB mouse Hallmark gene set collection (a mouse-specific Hallmark GMT with MGI symbols, staged in the reference store), restricting to sets with 15-500 members among the tested genes. Report NES, BH-adjusted p-values, and leading-edge genes for every significant set, and collapse redundant/overlapping significant sets to one representative each (keep the full table as supplement). State the gene set collection name/version, ranking metric, universe (tested genes), and size window explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Full tested gene list used as input, ranked by Wald statistic; no pre-thresholding
MSigDB mouse Hallmark GMT identified by version and gene-symbol space (MGI) in the output
Results table has NES, padj, leading-edge genes per hallmark set that passes the 15-500 size window
Redundant overlapping significant sets collapsed with one representative reported, full table kept as supplement

steps.question: What is the complete, reproducible summary of differentially expressed genes and enriched Hallmark pathways between HFD and chow mouse liver, including QC caveats about sample_01?

steps.description: Combine the QC findings (library size / PCA outcome for sample_01), the DESeq2 results table (gene counts tested, DE gene counts at padj<0.05, MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram), and the fgsea Hallmark results (significant pathways, NES, leading-edge genes) into one report. State the DESeq2 and fgsea package versions, the Hallmark collection version, the design formula and named contrast, the alpha and size-window thresholds, and set a random seed for any reproducibility-sensitive step. Include the enrichment-method-dependence caveat and the low-depth-sample caveat verbatim.
acceptance_criteria: Report includes method, package versions, design formula, contrast, thresholds, n_tested, n_DE genes, and session info
Report includes MA plot and dispersion plot with captions
Report includes fgsea Hallmark results with database version, ranking metric, universe, and size window stated
Report explicitly states the sample_01 low-depth caveat and the enrichment-method-dependence caveat

plan.title: Mouse liver HFD vs chow: DE genes and Hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: Raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 mouse liver samples: 6 high-fat diet, 6 chow, unpaired, single batch) are first checked for sample structure — one sample (sample_01) has a library size ~4x below the median and must be inspected, not silently dropped, per the low-depth-sample rule. DESeq2 then fits the standard two-group negative-binomial model (median-of-ratios normalization built into the model, explicit reference level = chow so a positive log2FC means higher in HFD) with a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples), a Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the fold change, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05 to call the differentially expressed genes. The Wald statistic from that fit ranks the full gene list (no threshold cut) for a preranked fgsea analysis against the MSigDB mouse Hallmark gene sets, giving the pathway-level answer to which hallmark programs shift with diet. A final report step consolidates both results with the QC diagnostics, the fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the leading-edge genes of significant hallmark sets, and the full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene set collection version, seed).

steps.method: vst(blind) PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size QC
keep gene with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (smallest group size)
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB mouse Hallmark
combined DE + GSEA report with diagnostics
